_comment: Cross-lane drift contract for the accessible name of a browser control. TWO independent implementations compute it: `accessibleName()` in extensions/chrome/src/lib/dom-adapter.ts (TypeScript, against a live Element) and `ACCESSIBLE_NAME_SOURCE` in packages/browser-actuator/src/inpage.ts (ES5 source evaluated inside the page, in Maman's own window). They cannot share code, and the name is the only handle an agent has on a control — a plan names its target, `confirm_name` re-states it, and discovery hands the agent back a string it will later send as a target. So a name computed in one lane MUST resolve in the other. Unlike the teach-egress and classifier contracts, this fixture is NOT generated by running one implementation: neither lane is authoritative, so the table below IS the specification and both suites assert against it. `rung` records which fallback produced the name; the suites also assert every rung is exercised, so deleting a rung fails rather than silently shrinking the table.

cases.html: Close date
cases.subject: #f
cases.why: accname resolves labelledby first. The in-page lane used to check aria-label first, so a field with both was named differently depending on which lane ran.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: The attribute is a list. The in-page lane used to pass the whole attribute to getElementById, which found nothing and fell through to a different rung entirely.

cases.html: Close date
cases.subject: #f
cases.why: A dangling reference contributes nothing rather than an empty segment, so the join does not produce stray spaces.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: A rung is used only when it yields text. Present-but-empty must not shadow the rungs below it.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: An explicit author-supplied name beats the native one.

cases.subject: input
cases.why: `a.b:c` is not a bare selector. Both lanes build a quoted attribute selector rather than interpolating the id into a compound one.

cases.subject: input
cases.why: The id closes the quoted attribute selector unless escaped. Both lanes escape backslash and double quote; the in-page lane used to escape only the quote.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: A placeholder is a format hint, not a name. Real forms carry both.

cases.html: <input id='f' type='submit' value='Save' title='Save the record'>
cases.subject: #f
cases.why: For a submit input the value attribute IS the native label; title is a tooltip about it. The extension lane used to rank title higher, so a button with both was named after its tooltip.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: The value rung is button types only. A date field named after its own contents would change name every time it was written to, and no stored plan could address it twice.

cases.html: <input id='f' placeholder='Close date' title='Pick a close date'>
cases.subject: #f
cases.why: The placeholder is on screen; the title only appears on hover.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: The in-page lane had no title rung at all, so an icon-only control named by its tooltip was addressable in one lane and not the other.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: THE divergence this contract exists for. The in-page lane ranked name above textContent and called this button 'save'; the extension called it 'Save and close'. A confirm_name written against either lane then refused in the other — a stop, but an unexplainable one.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: `name` is a form-submission key, not an accessible name in any spec. It stays because an otherwise-unnamed input is unaddressable without it, and an agent that receives the token from discovery can send it back verbatim.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: Empty rather than invented. An empty name matches nothing, which asks the user; a guessed one acts on the wrong element.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: A label wrapped across source lines must yield one string in both lanes. The in-page lane compares confirm_name by exact equality, so trimming the ends is not enough.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: Layout grids emit non-breaking spaces. They are presentation, and they are invisible in a diff.

cases.subject: #f
cases.why: Required-markers and trailing colons are stripped at MATCH time by normalizeName, not here. Both lanes must report the same raw name so the same normalisation applies to both.
